Subject: Orchid-12B onboarding: compatibility checks and temporary pin action plan

Team —

HorizonAI reached out with an on-demand request to onboard their new Orchid-12B family (orchid-12b / orchid-12b-int8) into our hosted catalog. They claim the int8 variant gives a 2.8x perf cost win vs their fp16, but R&D flagged some tokenization/LM-head variants that could affect safety/eval parity. 

Ask: I want a short, cross-functional plan so we can decide whether to:
- onboard immediately as an experimental variant behind a feature flag, or
- onboard but temporarily PIN serving to orchid-12b-fp16 for GA customers until compatibility & safety checks pass.

Please cover (quick bullets):
- infra constraints (RAM, GPU type, max batch) — Dev
- eval results & failure modes we've seen — Rishi
- security/compliance checklist (data flow, KMS, artifact provenance) — Neha
- product rollout proposal + risk tolerance (who gets access, canary size) — Grace
- account coordination (what HorizonAI will provide: checksum, reproducible artifact, S3 link) — Mateo

I attached the compatibility matrix HorizonAI sent and their perf run PDF. Can everyone reply by EOD Monday (11/16) with a single paragraph + any blocking asks? If any team needs more time, flag now and note the ETA.

Thanks —
Lauren
Senior PM, Platform
Redwood Inference

Lauren —

Quick infra readout after scanning the artifacts:
- The int8 artifact looks quantized for A100/RTX6000-class kernels; we'll need to validate on both Ampere and Hopper stacks. Memory footprint reported in PDF looks ~18GB vram / shard for 8k context in int8, which is acceptable for our mid-tier pools but will reduce packing efficiency.
- Key ask: provide a sample model shard and tokenizer file (small subset) so we can run a quick kernel-level smoke test. A full artifact link (signed) plus SHA256 would be ideal.
- If we pin to fp16 for GA traffic, we should still enable int8 in Dedicated pools under a separate model id to avoid unexpected fallback chaining.
- Potential rollout constraint: int8's KV cache behavior in our runtime is untested for 8k windows; expect some KV incompatibilities. Recommend a compatibility test matrix targeting sequence lengths 512, 2048, 8192.

Blocking: need the artifact URL + tokenizer + checksum. ETA for initial smoke tests: 48 hours after we get artifacts.

—Dev
Principal Infra Engineer

[Attachment requested: horizonai-artifact-checksum.txt]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Orchid-12B onboarding: compatibility checks and temporary pin action plan

TL;DR: Early eval shows tokenization drift and a small shift in hallucination rate on our diagnostic prompts. Recommend pin until we run regression sets.

Details:
- Ran the provided test vector (from the attached compat csv) locally on a copy of the int8 artifact (sanitized subset Horizon provided). Observed ~3.4% change in exact-match on our canonical QA set and a 1.5 pp increase in perplexity on long-form summarization tasks relative to our reference baseline (phoebe70b-sim).
- Tokenization: Orchid's tokenizer maps some rare unicode ligatures differently which causes subtle prompt truncation/misalignment in multi-turn. This is a safety/regression risk for evals that depend on token-level prompts.
- Failure modes to watch: coherence degradation on long context (>4k), occasional stray EOS tokens for specific control tokens we use for function-calling; needs a tokenizer alignment step or a model-side fix.

Recommendation: ship the model catalog entry but set a temporary serving PIN that routes production traffic to orchid-12b-fp16 by default for accounts with global rollout enabled. Allow private/dedicated customers to opt into int8 behind explicit toggle. Run full regression suite (we'll need 72 hrs compute after infra signoff).

—Rishi
Senior Applied Researcher

Security/compliance quick notes:
- Artifact provenance: we need a signed checksum (SHA256) and a simple SBOM-like manifest from HorizonAI listing build environment and third-party libs. The horizonai-artifact-checksum.txt file should be sent from their integration account and cross-signed if possible.
- Dataflow: confirm that no additional telemetry or hidden callbacks are enabled in the artifact. We require a declared network policy and a manifest of any external endpoints the model will contact at runtime (we block unknown egress by default).
- KMS/HSM: confirm that their model artifacts can be stored in our S3 buckets under our KMS key or that Horizon can provide an S3 presigned artifact with encryption-at-rest that meets our SOC2 policy.
- Compliance gating: if any of the above are missing, we cannot approve the int8 variant for hosted GA; it can remain in Dedicated or Private after an exception review.

Blocking: signed checksum + SBOM + network manifest.

—Neha
Security & Compliance Manager

Hi Redwood team —

Thanks for the fast coordination. Per Mateo's summary, we've uploaded the artifact and the checksum. A few clarifications:
- The int8 kernel is highly hardware-optimized; you should test on both A100 and H100 kernels. We included small driver hints in the SBOM.
- Tokenizer note: our tokenizer handles a few legacy ligature sequences differently for backward compatibility with earlier Orchid releases. We included a mapping table (see SBOM folder) and are happy to provide a conversion script if helpful.
- We agree to your request to flag the int8 variant as "experimental" by default in hosted and allow opt-in toggles for Dedicated customers. We will not promote int8 to GA until Redwood completes a regression sweep.

Attached: signed checksum and small artifact manifest. Let us know when infra can pull the artifact and we'll leave the link active for 72 hrs.

Thanks —
Luis Ferreira
Integrations Lead, HorizonAI
